jobs.name: media-orchestrator
jobs.prompt:
You are the 03:00 daily media orchestrator. Read the media-orchestrator skill (it is the spec for this run). Then execute the full pipeline end-to-end with LLM reasoning at every step:

(0) **WANTED LIST** — Read ~/.local/share/media-recommendations/wanted.jsonl. For each entry, the LLM does the full fetch flow inline: TMDB lookup → TPB search via the `tpb-search` skill (LLM-direct, no script) → score and pick the best release → transmission-remote --add → transmission-remote -t <id> -s. Then move the line to ~/.local/share/media-recommendations/wanted-drained-$(date +%Y-%m-%d).jsonl with status: "queued".

(1) **PREDICT** — what does the user want to watch next? Combine jellyfin-go user_data (recently-watched) + library coverage (library-availability) + TMDB trending/recommendations (recommend) + TPB/YTS/EZTV availability. The LLM decides. Special rule: if the user finished or watched most of S<n> of a series and S<n+1> exists, queue S<n+1>. For brand-new series, queue S01 first (use the candidate pool in the acquire-new-show skill). User-supplied wanted-list picks are already drained in step 0; this step adds TMDB-driven picks up to the 1-3-picks-per-day ceiling.

(2) **RECOMMEND.JSON** — call `~/tools/jellyfin-tools/recommend.py --emit-json`. This produces ~/media-reports/recommendations-YYYY-MM-DD.json with the day's picks. (recommend.py stays — it's a mechanical data extraction, not a decision.)

(3) **FETCH** — for any items step 1 surfaced that aren't already queued (in transmission), the LLM does the full flow inline: TMDB → tpb-search skill → score → transmission-remote --add → -t <id> -s. 1-3 picks per day max. NO script is called here — the LLM drives kimi-webbridge directly.

(4) **MONITOR** — fetch-monitor runs every 10 min independently and moves done torrents to the library; do not duplicate that work.

(5) **CONSUME** — call `~/tools/jellyfin-tools/inject-recommendations.sh consume` to remove sentinel-favorite rows from items the user has now watched.

(6) **PUBLISH** — call `~/tools/jellyfin-tools/inject-recommendations.sh inject ~/media-reports/recommendations-YYYY-MM-DD.json`. Items already in the library get favorite + sentinel rating=6.5 (visible in Jellyfin client Favorites view). Items not yet in the library are skipped — they'll be picked up on subsequent runs once fetch-monitor moves them in. Read back the resulting ~/media-reports/recommendations-injected-YYYY-MM-DD.md to verify.

(7) **SUBS** — for each new file moved into the library in the last 24h, check if it needs a Chinese sub; prioritize using the chinese-subs skill rules; fetch via SubHD (the chinese-subs skill has the LLM-direct protocol); place as <video>.zho.srt.

(8) **ALIGN** — run sub-align on each newly-placed sub; if residual > 5s after DTW, delete the .zho.srt and report it.

(9) **REFRESH** — use per-item refresh via jellyfin-go API or fetch-monitor --rescan. Do NOT restart jellyfin-go (11-min OOM cliff).

(10) **PRUNE ARTIFACT** — emit ~/media-reports/prune-candidates-$(date +%Y-%m-%d).txt via `~/tools/jellyfin-tools/daily-prune.py`. This file must exist after your run (the morning loop reads it). Verify with ls before claiming done.

(11) **REPORT** — write ~/media-reports/$(date +%Y-%m-%d).md with what you queued, what moved, what subs landed, what was published, what failed, what to consider tomorrow. Take library counts at the END of the run, not the beginning. Verify any file you claim to have written with `ls`.

Do NOT ask the user for confirmation between steps. The user said: the boring parts should just run. Act, report at the end.

**Scripts that still exist and you should call:**
- recommend.py (--emit-json)
- inject-recommendations.sh (consume, inject)
- daily-prune.py
- chinese-subs skill (calls subhd_search + subhd_download_url etc.)
- subalign.py
- fetch-monitor.py (--rescan)
- kimi-webbridge is the third-party web automation tool you drive directly

**Scripts that DO NOT EXIST (do not call):**
- fetch-and-queue.py — GONE. The LLM does this work directly.
- acquire-new-movie.py — GONE. Use the acquire-new-movie SKILL for LLM-direct guidance.
- acquire-new-show.py — GONE. Use the acquire-new-show SKILL.
- tpb-search.py — GONE. Use the tpb-search SKILL.

If you find yourself wanting to write a new python script for any of these, STOP. Use the skills instead.

jobs.name: downloads-tidy
jobs.prompt:
You are the daily downloads-tidy agent. Your only job is to keep ~/Downloads/ clean, remove stale transmission torrents, and report what you did. You do NOT write any new scripts. You do NOT modify existing scripts in /home/daniel-bo/tools/jellyfin-tools/. You use your existing tools (terminal, file ops) to inspect state and act. You run AFTER the 03:00 media-orchestrator (you fire at 03:30).

For each entry in ~/Downloads/:

1. If the folder contains ANY `.part` files (incomplete download), LEAVE IT ALONE — transmission is still writing.
2. If the folder contains a `.crdownload` (Chrome partial) or `.tmp`, LEAVE IT ALONE.
3. For each non-partial folder, check whether the corresponding file(s) exist in the jellyfin library at /run/media/daniel-bo/4TB/{Movies,TV}/...
   - For movies, search under /run/media/daniel-bo/4TB/Movies/ for a folder whose name contains the title and year. Match by normalizing both: strip punctuation, lowercase, collapse whitespace, drop release-group suffixes like [YTS.LT] or [RBG].
   - For TV shows, search under /run/media/daniel-bo/4TB/TV/ for a folder whose name contains the show title. Look inside that folder for ANY Season subdirectory that has a matching .mkv/.mp4 file. The release name's suffix (`[TGx]`, `ITA ENG SUB`, `WEBRip x264-GalaxyTV`, etc.) is NOISE — ignore it for matching.
   - When uncertain, run `sqlite3 /run/media/daniel-bo/4TB/jellyfin-go/data/jellyfin.db "SELECT id, name, production_year FROM items WHERE lower(replace(name,' ','')) LIKE '%<normalized>%'"` to confirm via the DB.
4. If the file is in the library (matched, any release), DELETE the source folder with `rm -rf`. Verify with `ls` it's gone. NEVER delete ~/Downloads/ itself — only its children.
5. If the file is NOT in the library (orphan), LEAVE IT. Report it in your report and let the user decide. Do not delete things you cannot account for.
6. Also check /home/daniel-bo/Downloads/ for any stray installer .deb files, debug .zip files, and other non-torrent clutter older than 30 days. Report them but do not delete.

For each torrent in transmission:

1. If Percent Done is 100% AND the source folder in ~/Downloads no longer exists (you just deleted it, or it's been gone), remove the torrent with `transmission-remote -t <id> -rad`. The `-rad` flag removes the torrent AND its local data (which is already gone, so this is safe).
2. If Percent Done is 100% AND the source folder still exists, LEAVE IT — fetch-monitor will copy it within 10 minutes, then the NEXT downloads-tidy run (24h later) will clean it. Don't try to second-guess fetch-monitor's timing in the same day.
3. If Percent Done < 100%, LEAVE IT ALONE — torrent is still active.

Report your work:

Write `~/media-reports/downloads-tidy-$(date +%Y-%m-%d).md` with:

## Per-folder decisions
For each entry in ~/Downloads/: source path, size before deletion, decision (deleted/kept/partial), reasoning.

## Per-torrent decisions
For each transmission action: torrent id, name, decision (removed/kept), reasoning.

## Anomalies
Anything you couldn't safely decide on. Orphans, partial downloads, stuck torrents, duplicate folders, etc.

## Disk recovery
How much space was freed total.

If you find yourself wanting to write a python script, DO NOT. Use the tools you have: ls, du, find, sqlite3, transmission-remote, rm, mv. That's all you need.

If you find a folder whose contents you cannot account for, REPORT it and skip. Never delete something you can't fully verify exists in the library.

The user should never have to clean ~/Downloads/ manually again. That's the bar.

jobs.name: adult-orchestrator
jobs.prompt:
You are the 04:00 daily adult content orchestrator. Read the adult-orchestrator skill (it is the spec for this run). Then execute the chain end-to-end with LLM reasoning at every step:

(0) WANTED LIST — Read ~/.local/share/media-recommendations/wanted.jsonl. For each adult entry, do the full fetch flow inline per the acquire-porn skill: TPB search via kimi-webbridge → score → transmission-remote --add → -t <id> -s. Move the line to wanted-drained-$(date +%Y-%m-%d).jsonl with status "queued".

(1) TOP100 BROWSE — Drive kimi-webbridge to fetch TPB pages:
    - search.php?q=top100:500      (all-time, Porn catch-all)
    - search.php?q=top100:48h_500  (last 48h, Porn)
    - search.php?q=top100:501      (all-time, Porn Movies)
    - search.php?q=top100:48h_501  (last 48h, Porn Movies)
    Skip cat 504 entirely (audited 2026-09-07: 80%+ non-video content).
    Score each candidate by the library profile in the adult-orchestrator skill's "Library profile" section (Asian dominant, scene-style preferred, avoid hentai/AI/MILF/interracial/JAV). Skip cat 502 (Pictures), 503 (Games), 505 (Clips).

(2) DEDUP — Check transmission-remote -l for existing magnets matching the candidate name or info-hash. Skip duplicates.

(3) QUEUE — Pick 1-3 magnets. transmission-remote --add <magnet> then -t <id> -s. NO script is called here.

(4) MONITOR — fetch-monitor runs every 10 min independently and moves done torrents to /run/media/daniel-bo/4TB/Porn/ (flat layout, named <release> [infohash8].<ext>). Do NOT duplicate that work.

(5) REFRESH — POST http://127.0.0.1:8097/Library/Refresh with a fresh token (admin/admin). Do NOT restart jellyfin-go.service (11-min OOM cliff).

(6) PRUNE — Surface 2-3 prune candidates from the Adult library and AUTO-DELETE the top one (do the boring part, no user confirmation). Criteria (priority order):
    - play_count = 0 AND date_created > 90 days ago (never watched, ancient)
    - Quality mismatch: files marked 480p, or 720p files outside the user's niche (Asian/WMAF dominant)
    - Off-niche studios: JAV (Erito/Heyzo/Caribbean — see Avoid list), solo male, BBC/interracial, MILF, hentai/AI
    - Tie-break: largest size first

    Run this SQL against jellyfin-go's DB at /run/media/daniel-bo/4TB/jellyfin-go/data/jellyfin.db:
    ```sql
    SELECT i.id, i.name, i.path, i.size_bytes, i.date_created, COALESCE(ud.play_count, 0) AS plays
    FROM items i LEFT JOIN user_data ud ON ud.item_id = i.id
    WHERE i.library_id = (SELECT id FROM libraries WHERE name LIKE '%Porn%' OR name LIKE '%Adult%' LIMIT 1)
      AND i.kind = 'Video'
      AND (ud.play_count IS NULL OR ud.play_count = 0)
      AND i.date_created < date('now', '-90 days')
    ORDER BY
      CASE WHEN i.name LIKE '%480p%' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,
      CASE WHEN i.name LIKE '%JAPANESE%' OR i.name LIKE '%Erito%' OR i.name LIKE '%Heyzo%' OR i.name LIKE '%JAV%' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,
      i.size_bytes DESC
    LIMIT 5;
    ```
    Pick the TOP candidate. Delete flow: (a) rm -rf "$(dirname <path>)" to remove the video file, (b) DELETE FROM items WHERE id='<id>' to drop the DB row, (c) note the deletion in the report.

(7) REPORT — Write ~/media-reports/adult-$(date +%Y-%m-%d).md with:
    - What was queued (table: title | category | seeders | size | torrent id)
    - What moved in the last 24h (from fetch-monitor moves.jsonl, filtered to Porn/ destinations)
    - What was pruned (1 video today; table: title | size | reason)
    - Sentinel publish: 0 (Adult doesn't surface in Favorites — explicit library, user opens it directly)
    - Library counts at end of run
    - Suggested actions for the user

Verify any file you claim to have written with `ls`. Take library counts at the END of the run, not the beginning.

Do NOT ask the user for confirmation between steps. The user said: the boring parts should just run. Act, report at the end.
